Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 59, verses 1–5:

Medinan. It has twenty-four verses, four hundred and forty-five words, and nine hundred and thirteen letters.

Abu al-'Abbas Sahl ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id al-Marwazi informed us, saying: Abu al-Hasan al-Mahmudi related to me by reading: Tamim ibn Mahmud related to us from al-'Abbas ibn [ ... ] [[Word not legible.]] from his men, saying: Muhammad ibn Salih related to us from Zayd al-'Ajami from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Prophet ﷺ (peace be upon him) said: "Whoever recites Surat al-Hashr, no Paradise, no Fire, no Throne, no Footstool, no veil, no seven heavens, no seven earths, no creeping things, wind, birds, trees, beasts, mountains, sun, moon, or angels will remain without sending blessings upon him and asking forgiveness for him. If he dies that same day or night, he dies a martyr." [247] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 9/423.]]

In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth glorifies God, and He is the Mighty, the Wise. He it is who expelled those who disbelieved among the People of the Book from their homes at the first gathering...﴾ etc.

The exegetes said: These verses in their entirety were revealed concerning the Banu al-Nadir, and that is because the Prophet ﷺ, when he entered Medina, was given a treaty by the Banu al-Nadir that they would not fight him nor fight alongside him, and the Messenger of God ﷺ accepted this from them. When the Messenger of God ﷺ campaigned at Badr and prevailed over the polytheists, the Banu al-Nadir said: "By God, he is indeed the Prophet whose description we found in the Torah: his banner will not be turned back." When the Messenger of God ﷺ campaigned at Uhud and the Muslims were defeated, they doubted and became hypocrites, showing enmity toward the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) and the believers, and they broke the covenant that existed between them and the Messenger of God ﷺ. Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf rode out with forty riders from the Jews to Mecca, and they came to the Quraysh, allied with them, and bound themselves to them that their word would be one against Muhammad (peace be upon him). Then Abu Sufyan entered the mosque with forty men, and Ka'b with forty Jews, and they took a pledge from one another between the curtains and the Ka'bah. Then Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf and his companions returned to Medina, and Gabriel descended upon the Messenger of God ﷺ and informed him of what Ka'b and Abu Sufyan had agreed upon. He (peace be upon him) ordered the killing of Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf, and Muhammad ibn Maslamah al-Ansari killed him, and he was his foster-brother.

The Messenger of God ﷺ had already become aware of their treachery and breach of covenant, until the Messenger of God ﷺ came to them, accompanied by Abu Bakr, 'Umar and 'Ali (may God be pleased with them), seeking their help regarding the blood-money of the two Muslim men whom 'Amr ibn Umayyah al-Damri killed on his return from Bi'r Ma'unah, when they had been sent to the Banu 'Amir. They agreed to his request, seated him, and then intended to assassinate him and throw a stone upon him from the top of the fortress, but God, glorified is He, informed him of this and protected him.

This story has passed, along with the story of the killing of Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf. When Ka'b was killed, the Messenger of God ﷺ rose in the morning and commanded the people to march against the Banu al-Nadir, who were at a village of theirs called Zuhrah. When the Prophet ﷺ advanced toward them, he found them wailing over Ka'b, who had been their chief, and they said: "O Muhammad, cry upon cry after cry, and weeping after weeping?" He said: "Yes." They said: "Leave us to weep for our dead, then we will consider your command." The Prophet ﷺ said: "Leave the city." [248] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 18/4, with variation.]]

They said: "Death is nearer to us than that."

So they called to war and declared the fight, and the hypocrites, 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy and his companions, sent to them: "Do not leave the fortress; if they fight you, we are with you, we will not forsake you, and we will surely support you, and if you are expelled, we will surely go out with you." So they fortified the alleys and their fortresses. Then they resolved to betray the Messenger of God ﷺ and sent to him: "Go out with thirty men of your companions, and let thirty men of ours go out, until we meet at a place midway between us and you, and they will hear from you; if they believe you and have faith in you, we will all believe."

The Prophet ﷺ went out with thirty of his companions, and thirty rabbis of the Jews went out to him. When they were in an open place, some of the Jews said to others: "How can we get at him while there are thirty men of his companions with him, all of whom wish to die before him?" They sent to him: "How can we understand while we are sixty men? Go out with three of your companions, and we will bring out three of our scholars, and they will hear from you; if they believe in you, we will all believe in you and confirm you."

The Prophet ﷺ went out with three of his companions, and three Jews went out, and they concealed daggers and intended to assassinate the Messenger of God ﷺ. A sincere woman from the Banu al-Nadir sent to her brother, who was a Muslim man of the Ansar, and informed him of what the Banu al-Nadir intended of treachery against the Messenger of God (peace be upon him). Her brother came quickly until he reached the Prophet ﷺ and whispered to him the news of them before the Prophet ﷺ arrived, and the Prophet ﷺ (peace be upon him) returned.

When the next day came, he advanced upon them with the battalions and besieged them for twenty-one nights. When God, glorified is He, cast terror into their hearts, and they despaired of the help of the hypocrites, they asked the Prophet of God (peace be upon him) for reconciliation, but he refused them [except] [[In the manuscript it reads (an la).]] that they should leave Medina according to what the Prophet ﷺ commanded them. They accepted this, and he made peace with them on the basis of exile, on the condition that they may take whatever their camels could carry of their property, except the weapons (al-hilqah), and that they leave to him their homes, their estates, and all their other property.

Ibn 'Abbas said: He made peace with them on the condition that each household could load three houses' worth of goods onto a camel, whatever goods they wished, and the rest belonged to the Prophet ﷺ.

al-Dahhak said: He gave every three persons a camel and a waterskin. They did this and left Medina for Syria, to Adhri'at and Ariha, except two households among them: the family of Abu al-Huqayq and the family of Huyayy ibn Akhtab, who joined Khaybar, and a group of them joined al-Hirah. This is the saying of God, exalted and sublime: ﴿He it is who expelled those who disbelieved among the People of the Book﴾, meaning the Banu al-Nadir, ﴿from their homes﴾, which were in Yathrib.

Ibn Ishaq said: The expulsion of the Banu al-Nadir occurred upon the Prophet's ﷺ return from Uhud, and the conquest of Qurayzah was upon his return from the Confederates, and there were two years between them.

﴿At the first gathering﴾. al-Zuhri said: They were of a tribe that had never been exiled before, and God, glorified is He, had decreed exile upon them; had it not been for that, He would have punished them in this world. They were the first gathering in this world; they were gathered to Syria.

Ibn 'Abbas said: Whoever doubts that the gathering place is in Syria, let him recite this verse. The Prophet ﷺ said to them that day: "Go out." They said: "To where?" He said: "To the land of the gathering," and God, glorified is He, revealed ﴿at the first gathering﴾.

al-Kalbi said: He said ﴿at the first gathering﴾ only because they were the first of the People of the Book to be gathered and expelled from the Hijaz.

Murrah al-Hamdani said: This was the first gathering from Medina, and the second gathering was from Khaybar and the whole Arabian Peninsula to Adhri'at and Ariha in Syria, in the days of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may God be pleased with him), and upon his body [[Thus in the manuscript.]].

Qatadah said: This was the first gathering, and the second gathering is a fire that gathers them from the east to the west; it spends the night with them wherever they spend the night, and it rests with them wherever they rest, and it devours whoever lags behind among them.

Yaman ibn Rabab said: He only said ﴿at the first gathering﴾ because God, glorified is He, granted victory to His Prophet (peace be upon him) at the first time he fought them.

﴿You did not think, O believers, that they would leave, and they thought that their fortresses would protect them from God﴾, in that they had made them into alleys and fortified them. ﴿But God came upon them from where they did not reckon﴾, that is, the command of God and His justice. ﴿And He cast terror into their hearts﴾ by the killing of their chief Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf.

﴿They destroyed their houses﴾ — the common reading is with the light form, from ikhrab, meaning they demolish. Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, al-Hasan al-Basri and Abu 'Amr ibn al-'Ala read it with the intensive form, from takhrib. Abu 'Amr said: I chose the intensive form because ikhrab means leaving a thing in ruins without an inhabitant, and the Banu al-Nadir did not leave their dwellings so that they could move away from them; rather, they ruined them by tearing out and demolishing.

Others said: takhrib and ikhrab have the same meaning.

al-Zuhri said: That is because when the Prophet ﷺ made peace with them on the condition that they may take whatever their camels could carry, they would look at a piece of wood in their houses that they admired, or a pillar or a door, and they would demolish their houses, pull them out, load them onto their camels, and the believers would ruin what remained.

Ibn Zayd said: They would uproot the pillars, tear down the roofs, break through the walls, and pull out the wood, even the pegs, ruining them so that the believers would not dwell in them, out of envy and hatred.

al-Dahhak said: Whenever the Muslims demolished any of their fortifications, they themselves would tear down their houses with their own hands and ruin them, and then they would seek what the Muslims had ruined.

Ibn 'Abbas said: Whenever the Muslims gained control of one of their houses, they demolished it so that the field of combat would be wider for them; and the enemies of God would break through their houses from the back, emerging into the next one, fortifying themselves in it and breaking what was near them, and throwing what they had left upon the companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ. [[See Tarikh al-Islam by al-Dhahabi: Section on the Campaigns, p. 122.]]

Qatadah said: The Muslims would ruin what was adjacent to them from the outside, and the Jews would ruin them from the inside. This is the saying of God, exalted and sublime: ﴿They destroyed their houses with their own hands and the hands of the believers, so take warning, O people of insight﴾,

meaning: be admonished, O you who possess intellects.

﴿And had it not been that God had decreed for them the exile﴾, that is, leaving their homeland, ﴿He would have punished them in this world﴾ with killing and captivity, as He did to the Banu Qurayzah. ﴿And for them in the Hereafter is the punishment of the Fire. That is because they opposed God and His Messenger, and whoever opposes God — indeed, God is severe in penalty.﴾ Talhah ibn Musarrif read: (wa man yushāqqi Allāh), like the one in al-Anfal.

﴿Whatever palm trees you cut down, or left standing on their roots...﴾ — the verse. This was because when the Messenger of God ﷺ arrived at the Banu al-Nadir and they had fortified themselves in their fortresses, he ordered that their palm trees be cut down and burned. The enemies of God were distressed at this and said: "O Muhammad, you claimed you wanted reform. Is cutting down trees and felling palms part of reform? Did you find in what you claimed was revealed to you corruption in the earth?" This grieved the Prophet ﷺ, and the Muslims were troubled by their words, and feared that this might be corruption. The Muslims differed about it: some said, "Do not cut them down, for they are part of what God has granted us as spoils," and others said, "Rather, we will enrage them by cutting them down." So God, glorified is He, revealed this verse, confirming the one who forbade cutting them and declaring lawful the one who cut them, free of sin, and informed that cutting them and leaving them is by the permission of God, glorified is He.

Abu 'Abd Allah Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah, Abu Muhammad Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, Abu 'Ali al-Hasan ibn Muhammad and Abu al-Qasim al-Hasan ibn Muhammad informed us, saying: Abu al-'Abbas al-Asamm related to us, saying: al-Rabi' informed us, saying:

al-Shafi'i informed us, from Malik, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, that the Prophet ﷺ ordered the burning of the palm trees of the Banu al-Nadir, and Hassan ibn Thabit said about it:

"And it was nothing to the nobles of the Banu Lu'ayy... a blaze at al-Buwayrah spreading far."
[[Lisan al-'Arab: 4/513.]]

And concerning that, God, glorified is He, revealed: ﴿Whatever palm trees you cut down﴾.

The scholars differed about the word līnah: some said it refers to palms other than the ajwah, so that all palms except the ajwah are līnah; this is the view of 'Ikrimah, Yazid ibn Ruwan and Qatadah.

It is related from Badhan from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Prophet ﷺ had commanded the cutting of their palms except the ajwah.

The people of Medina call the dates other than the ajwah "al-alwan" (the varieties), its singular being lawn and līnah, and its origin is lawnah, and the waw was changed to yā' because of the kasrah before it.

al-Zuhri said: līnah is all the varieties of palm except the ajwah and the barniyyah. Mujahid, 'Atiyyah and Ibn Zayd said: it is all palms without exception.

al-'Awfi from Ibn 'Abbas: it is a variety of palm.

Abu 'Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Muzani informed us, saying: al-Hadrami related to us, saying: Ja'far ibn Muhammad related to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak related to us, from 'Uthman ibn 'Ata', from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His words ﴿whatever palm trees you cut down﴾, he said: the palm and the tree.

Sufyan said: It is the noble palms.

Muqatil said: It is a kind of palm whose fruit is called lawn, which is intensely yellow, with its seed visible from outside, and the molar tooth sinks into it. It was among their finest dates and the most pleasing to them. A single palm of this kind was worth a slave-boy, and dearer to them than a slave-boy. When they saw that kind being cut down, it grieved them greatly, and they said to the believers: "You claim you dislike corruption, yet you spread corruption, ruin and cut down trees. Leave these palms, for they belong to whoever prevails over them."

It was also said: it is the palm close to the ground.

al-Akhfash recited:

"The dove has stirred me when it sang, parting from the beloved, from atop the līnah."
[[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 18/9.]]

The Arabs call all varieties of palm līnah. Dhu al-Rummah said:

"As if my saddle-frame above her were a bird's nest, upon a līnah, whose flanks flutter..."

And he also said:

"Striking with her remaining feathers, settling upon a līnah, at night, in its plumage glistening."
[[Lisan al-'Arab: 8/139.]]

The plural of līnah is līn, and it was said līyān. Imru' al-Qays, describing the neck of a horse, said:

"And a neck like the palm-fibre ropes, which the fiery one set alight."

﴿Or you left them standing on their roots﴾: their trunks, so you did not cut them down nor burn them. 'Abd Allah read: (Whatever palm you cut down or left, none of the people was left standing on their roots except by the permission of God). al-A'mash read: (Whatever palm you cut down or left standing qawwam on their roots).

﴿So by the permission of God, and that He might disgrace the defiantly disobedient﴾, that is, that He might humiliate the Jews and grieve and enrage them.

**Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 59, verses 6–7:**

*"And what Allah restored (afā'a) to His Messenger"*: Allah returned it to His Messenger and gave it back to him. From the same root is *fay' al-ẓill* (the shade's return). *"From them"*: from the Banu al-Nadir, in terms of wealth. *"You did not make your horses or camels charge (awjaftum)"*: you did not urge horses or *rikāb* (riding camels) against it. *Rikāb* means camels. He said:

They did not cover any distance to reach it, nor did they suffer any hardship in it, nor were they burdened with any expense, nor did they face any battle. It was in Medina, so they walked to it on foot. They did not ride horses or camels, except the Prophet (ﷺ), who rode a camel. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took it by treaty (ṣulḥan), expelled them from it, and secured their wealth. The believers asked the Prophet (ﷺ) to divide it. Then Allah, glorified is He, revealed: ﴿Whatever Allah restored to His Messenger from them, you did not make horses or camels charge against it, but Allah gives His messengers power over whom He wills, and Allah is over all things competent﴾. So Allah made the wealth of the Banu al-Nadir exclusively for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), to place wherever he wished. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) divided it among the Emigrants (Muhajirun) and gave the Helpers (Ansar) none of it, except three men who were in need: Abu Dujana Simak ibn Kharasha, Sahl ibn Hunayf, and al-Harith ibn al-Simma. Of the Banu al-Nadir, only two men became Muslim: one was Sufyan ibn Umayr ibn Wahb, and the other was Sa'id ibn Wahb. They both kept their wealth and secured it.

We were informed by Abdullah ibn Hamid, who said: Hamid ibn Muhammad informed us, who said: Bishr ibn Musa informed us, who said:

Al-Humaydi told us, who said: Sufyan told us, who said: Amr ibn Dinar and Ma'mar ibn Rashid told us, from Ibn Shihab al-Zuhri, that he heard Malik ibn Aws ibn al-Hadathan al-Basri say: I heard Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) say: The wealth of the Banu al-Nadir was among what Allah restored to His Messenger, which the Muslims did not charge against with horses or camels, so it was exclusively for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) would spend from it on his family for a year's provision, and what remained he placed in horses and weapons as provision in the way of Allah.

We were informed by Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Hamdun, who said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan informed us, who said: Muhammad ibn Yahya told us, who said: Muhammad ibn Yusuf told us, who said: Ibn Uyayna told us, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, who said: And I was informed [[Beginning of a second chain to al-Zuhri.]] from Muhammad ibn Jarir, who said: My father told us, who said: Abd al-A'la told us, who said: Abu Thawr told us, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, from Malik ibn Aws ibn al-Hadathan, who said: Umar ibn al-Khattab sent for me, so I entered upon him. He said: Some people from your tribe who are of the "Thabat" (a group of fighters) have come, and we have ordered a gratuity (rad̲kh) for them, so divide it among them.

I said: O Commander of the Faithful, command someone other than me to do that. He said: Take it, O man.

While I was in that state, his client Yarfa' came and said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, al-Zubayr, Uthman, and Sa'd are asking permission to enter. He said: Admit them. Then he remained a while, then came and said: Ali and al-Abbas are asking permission. He said: Admit them. When al-Abbas entered, he said: O Commander of the Faithful, judge between me and this treacherous, sinful, deceitful one!!! [[What al-Abbas attributed indicates a lack of manners on his part, since no Muslim should deny the virtue of Ali ibn Abi Talib in Islam, let alone al-Abbas, the uncle of the Messenger (ﷺ). If this indicates anything, it indicates only that this narration was fabricated. Among the narrations built on this are:

Ahmad and al-Hakim narrated, and he authenticated it, from Umm Salama, who said: I heard the Prophet (ﷺ) say: "Whoever reviles Ali has reviled me."

Al-Tabarani narrated with a sound chain from Umm Salama, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that he said: "Whoever loves Ali has loved me, and whoever loves me has loved Allah, and whoever hates Ali has hated me, and whoever hates me has hated Allah."

Refer to Tarikh Dimashq (42/266–270) and its chains.]]. At that time they were disputing about what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, restored to His Messenger from the wealth of the Banu al-Nadir. The people said: Judge between them, O Commander of the Faithful, and relieve each of them from the other, for their dispute has lasted long. He said: I ask you by Allah, by whose permission the heavens and the earth stand: Do you know that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "We do not leave inheritance; what we leave is charity"? [250] [[Musnad Ahmad: 1/6.]]

They said: He did say that. Then he said to the two of them: Do you know that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said that? They said: Yes.

He said: I will inform you about this *fay'*. Allah, glorified is He, singled out His Prophet (peace be upon him) with something He did not give to anyone else, when He said, Mighty is He who speaks: ﴿Whatever Allah restored to His Messenger from them, you did not make horses or camels charge against it﴾. So this was exclusively for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him). By Allah, he did not choose it over you, nor did he hoard it over you. He divided it among you until only this wealth remained, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would spend from it on his family for their year's provision, then he would place what remained in the wealth of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

﴿Whatever Allah restored to His Messenger from the people of the townships﴾: meaning, from the wealth of the disbelievers, the people of the townships.

Ibn Abbas said: They are Qurayza and al-Nadir, both in Medina; Fadak, which is three miles from Medina; Khaybar; the villages of Urayna; and Yanbu'. Allah, exalted is He, made them for His Messenger to judge concerning them as he wished, and he took them all. Some people said: Why did he not divide them? So Allah, glorified is He, revealed this verse: ﴿Whatever Allah restored to His Messenger from the people of the townships﴾.

﴿…belongs to Allah and to the Messenger and to the kinsmen (dhi al-qurba)﴾: the relatives of the Prophet (ﷺ), who are the Banu Hashim and the Banu al-Muttalib.

The jurists differed concerning the basis of their entitlement to their share of *fay'* and *ghanima* (spoils of war).

Some people said: They are entitled to it by kinship, and need or lack of need is not a consideration regarding them. This is the view of al-Shafi'i and his companions.

Others said: They are entitled to it by need, not kinship. This is the view of Abu Hanifa and his companions. So when it is divided among them, males receive more than females, as in the ruling of inheritance: a male receives two shares and a female one.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: He made them equal, and males are not given more than females.

Mention of the ruling of these two verses.

The scholars differed concerning it. Some said: By His saying, ﴿Whatever Allah restored to His Messenger from the people of the townships﴾, He meant the spoils that Muslims take from the wealth of the disbelievers by force and compulsion. At the beginning of Islam the spoils belonged to those whom Allah, glorified is He, named in Surat al-Hashr, not to those who took them or charged against them. Then this was abrogated (*nasakha*, abrogation) by His saying in Surat al-Anfal: ﴿And know that whatever you obtain of anything…﴾, to the end of the verse.

This is the view of Yazid ibn Ruyan and Qatada.

Others said: The first verse explains the ruling on the wealth of the Banu al-Nadir specifically, because of His saying: ﴿Whatever Allah restored to His Messenger from them﴾. The second verse explains the ruling on all other wealth that was obtained without fighting and without charging against it with horses or camels.

Others said: They are one, and the second verse explains the division of the wealth that Allah, glorified is He, mentioned in the first verse.

Know that the total of the wealth in which rulers and governors have a share is of three kinds:

The first: what is taken from the Muslims as a means of purifying them, such as *sadaqat* (charities).

The second: the *ghanima* (spoils), which is what comes into the hands of the Muslims from the wealth of the disbelievers through war or treaty.

The third: the *fay'*, which is what returned to the Prophet (ﷺ) from the wealth of the disbelievers, freely and purely, without fighting or charging against it with horses and camels. Examples are the wealth of peace treaties, the *jizya* (poll tax), the *kharaj* (land tax), and the *'ushur* (tithes) taken from the merchants of the disbelievers when they enter the abode of Islam; and when the polytheists flee and leave their wealth, or one of them dies in the abode of Islam and has no heir.

As for the *sadaqat*, their disbursement is what Allah, glorified and exalted is He, mentioned: ﴿Charities are only for the poor﴾ [[Surat al-Tawba: 60.]], to the end of the verse. The explanation of the two categories of recipients has already passed.

As for the *ghanima*, at the beginning of Islam it belonged to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), to do with as he wished, as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Say: the spoils belong to Allah and the Messenger﴾ [[Surat al-Anfal: 1.]]. Then this was abrogated by His saying: ﴿And know that whatever you obtain of anything﴾, to the end of the verse. So four-fifths of it was made for those who obtained it, to be divided among them.

As for money, goods, commodities, garments, animals, and horses and camels, they are divided among them and not withheld from them.

As for real estate, the jurists differed concerning it. Malik (may Allah have mercy on him) said: The imam may withhold the lands from them and make them a *waqf* (endowment) for the public interests of the Muslims.

Abu Hanifa said: The imam has the choice between dividing them among them or withholding them from them and making them a *waqf* for the public interests of the Muslims.

Al-Shafi'i (may Allah be pleased with him) said: The imam may not withhold them from them without their consent, and their ruling is the ruling of all other wealth.

This is the preferred view, because Allah, glorified is He, removed the *khums* (one-fifth) from it after attributing the whole to them by His saying: ﴿you obtained﴾. This indicates that the remainder belongs to them and is their right. As for the remaining one-fifth, it is divided into five shares: one share for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), one share for the kinsmen (dhi al-qurba), one share for orphans, one share for the needy, and one share for the wayfarer (ibn al-sabil).

As for the *fay'*, during the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) it was divided into twenty-five shares: four-fifths of it, which is twenty shares, belonged to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), to do with as he wished and to decide concerning as he willed; and the remaining one-fifth was divided according to the division of the one-fifth of the *ghanima*.

After the death of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), the jurists differed concerning the four-fifths that had been his (ﷺ) from the *fay'*.

Some said: They are to be spent on the fighters who devote themselves to combat on the frontiers (*thughur*). This is one of the two opinions of al-Shafi'i (may Allah be pleased with him).

Others said: They are to be spent on the public interests of the Muslims, such as securing the frontiers, digging wells, building bridges, and the like, beginning with the most important and then the next most important. This is al-Shafi'i's other opinion (may Allah be pleased with him).

As for the share that belonged to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) from the one-fifth of the *fay'* and the one-fifth of the *ghanima*, it is spent after him on the public interests of the Muslims without disagreement, as he (ﷺ) said: "The *khums* is returned to you (to be spent among you)" [251] [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 4/372, no. 10967.]].

Likewise, what he left of wealth that is not inherited from him, rather it is charity, which is spent after him on the public interests of the Muslims, as he (ﷺ) said: "We do not leave inheritance; what we leave is charity" [252] [[Sahih Muslim: 5/152.]].

So the Messenger of Allah's (ﷺ) *safaya* (exclusive properties) from the *fay'* wealth, which Allah, glorified is He, singled out for him, were what he spent on his family for a year's provision, and what remained he placed in horses and weapons in the way of Allah, as mentioned. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) died, Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) took charge of them and did with them what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to do. Then Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) took charge of them in the manner in which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and Abu Bakr had managed them. When Uthman was appointed caliph, he entrusted them to Ali ibn Abi Talib by way of delegation, and made him the one who divides them. He managed them as the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) and his two companions had managed them. And success is from Allah.

We were informed by Aqil that Abu al-Faraj informed them, from Abu Ja'far al-Tabari, who said: Ibn Abd al-A'la told us, who said:

Ibn Thawr told us, from Ma'mar, from Ayyub, from Ikrima ibn Khalid, from Malik ibn Aws ibn al-Hadathan, who said: Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) recited: ﴿The charities are only for the poor﴾ until he reached ﴿Knowing and Wise﴾ [[Surat al-Tawba: 60.]]. Then he said: This is for these. Then he recited ﴿And know that whatever you obtain of anything, then for Allah is one-fifth of it﴾ [[Surat al-Anfal: 41.]], to the end of the verse. Then he said: This is for these. Then he recited ﴿Whatever Allah restored to His Messenger from the people of the townships﴾ until he reached ﴿for the poor emigrants … and those who were settled (in the abode) before them … and those who came after them﴾. Then he said: These verses have encompassed all Muslims generally, so there is no one who does not have a right in them. Then he said: If I live, the shepherd will come, while he is herding his donkeys, and his share from it will reach him without his brow having sweated for it [[From Tafsir al-Tabari 28:37; in the manuscript: "and his donkeys will reach it."]].

**﴿So that it does not become a circulating commodity (dūlah) among the rich﴾**: The reading of the common readers is *yakūna* (with the *yā'*) and *dūlatan* (in the accusative), meaning "so that the *fay'* does not become a circulating commodity." Abu Ja'far read it with *tā'* and in the nominative, meaning "so that the spoils or wealth do not become..." He made *dūlatun* the subject of *kāna* (was), and took the verb *kāna* in the sense of "occur," so it has no predicate. All the readers read the *dāl* of *dūlatan* with a *ḍamma* (u) except Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, who read its *dāl* with a *fatḥa* (a).

Isa ibn Umar said: The two forms have the same meaning. Others distinguished between them: *dawlah* (with *fatḥa*) means victory and dominance in war and other matters, and it is a verbal noun; *dūlah* (with *ḍamma*) is the name of the thing that people circulate among themselves, like a loan. The meaning of the verse is: so that the *fay'* does not become a circulating commodity among leaders, the powerful, and the wealthy, who would overcome the poor and the weak with it. This is because in the pre-Islamic period, when they obtained booty, the chief would take a quarter of it for himself, called *al-mirbā'*, and then select from it also—i.e. (*'adā*, the *mirbā'*) [[Thus in the manuscript; the likely reading is "*'adā*".]]—whatever he wished. About this their poet said:

For you is the *mirbā'* from it, and the *ṣafāyā*, and your judgment, and the *nashīṭa* and the *fuḍūl* [[Lisan al-'Arab: 7/415.]].

So Allah, glorified is He, made the Messenger's (peace be upon him) command regarding its division in the places where he was commanded, with no *khums* in them. When the *khums* is removed, it is lifted from all Muslims.

**﴿And whatever the Messenger gives you﴾**: what he gives you of the *fay'* and the *ghanima* ﴿take it﴾; ﴿and whatever he forbids you from﴾, such as embezzlement (*ghulūl*) and other things, ﴿refrain from it﴾. [*Ghulūl* is embezzlement specifically in the spoils. *Al-Ṣiḥāḥ* 5:1784, root *gh-l*.]

Al-Hasan said concerning this verse: He gives them the spoils and prevents them from embezzlement.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, who said: Abu Hudhayfa Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ali told us, who said: Abu Muhammad Ubayd ibn Ahmad ibn Ubayd al-Ṣaffar al-Ḥimṣī told us, who said: Aṭiyya ibn Baqiyya ibn al-Walid told us, who said: Isa ibn Abi Isa told us, who said: Musa ibn Abi Habib told us, who said: I heard al-Hakam ibn Umayr al-Thumali—and he had companionship with the Prophet—say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "This Qur'an is difficult, hard to grasp, heavy upon those who abandon it, and easy for those who follow and seek it. My speech (ḥadīth) is also difficult, hard to grasp, and it is the ruling (al-ḥukm). Whoever holds fast to my speech and memorizes it, is saved along with the Qur'an. Whoever neglects the Qur'an and my speech loses this world and the Hereafter. You have been commanded to take my word, to hold fast to my command, and to follow my Sunna. Whoever is pleased with my word has been pleased with the Qur'an, and whoever mocks my word has mocked the Qur'an. Allah, glorified is He, said: ﴿Whatever the Messenger gives you, take it, and whatever he forbids you, refrain from it﴾" [253] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 18/17.]].

We were informed by al-Husayn, who said: Ibn Shanbah told us, who said: al-Firyabi and Ubayd Allah ibn Ahmad al-Kinani told us, both saying: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shayba told us, who said: Mu'awiya ibn Hisham told us, who said: Sufyan al-Thawri told us, from al-Ashtar, from Ibrahim, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid, who said: Abdullah ibn Mas'ud met a man in the state of *ihram*, wearing his clothes, and said: Take them off. The man said: Are you reciting to me a verse from the Book of Allah with this? He said: Yes: ﴿Whatever the Messenger gives you, take it, and whatever he forbids you, refrain from it﴾ [254].

﴿And fear Allah; indeed, Allah is severe in punishment.﴾

From the same root is *fay' al-ẓill* (the shade's return). *"From them"*: from the Banu al-Nadir, in terms of wealth. *"You did not make your horses or camels charge (awjaftum)"*: you did not urge horses or *rikāb* (riding camels) against it. *Rikāb* means camels. He said:

They did not cover any distance to reach it, nor did they suffer any hardship in it, nor were they burdened with any expense, nor did they face any battle. It was in Medina, so they walked to it on foot. They did not ride horses or camels, except the Prophet (ﷺ), who rode a camel. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took it by treaty (ṣulḥan), expelled them from it, and secured their wealth. The believers asked the Prophet (ﷺ) to divide it. Others distinguished between them: *dawlah* (with *fatḥa*) means victory and dominance in war and other matters, and it is a verbal noun; *dūlah* (with *ḍamma*) is the name of the thing that people circulate among themselves, like a loan. The meaning of the verse is: so that the *fay'* does not become a circulating commodity among leaders, the powerful, and the wealthy, who would overcome the poor and the weak with it. This is because in the pre-Islamic period, when they obtained booty, the chief would take a quarter of it for himself, called *al-mirbā'*, and then select from it also—i.e. (*'adā*, the *mirbā'*) [[Thus in the manuscript; the likely reading is "*'adā*".]]—whatever he wished. About this their poet said:

For you is the *mirbā'* from it, and the *ṣafāyā*, and your judgment, and the *nashīṭa* and the *fuḍūl* [[Lisan al-'Arab: 7/415.]].

So Allah, glorified is He, made the Messenger's (peace be upon him) command regarding its division in the places where he was commanded, with no *khums* in them. When the *khums* is removed, it is lifted from all Muslims.

**﴿And whatever the Messenger gives you﴾**: what he gives you of the *fay'* and the *ghanima* ﴿take it﴾; ﴿and whatever he forbids you from﴾, such as embezzlement (*ghulūl*) and other things, ﴿refrain from it﴾. [*Ghulūl* is embezzlement specifically in the spoils. *Al-Ṣiḥāḥ* 5:1784, root *gh-l*.]

Al-Hasan said concerning this verse: He gives them the spoils and prevents them from embezzlement.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, who said: Abu Hudhayfa Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ali told us, who said: Abu Muhammad Ubayd ibn Ahmad ibn Ubayd al-Ṣaffar al-Ḥimṣī told us, who said: Aṭiyya ibn Baqiyya ibn al-Walid told us, who said: Isa ibn Abi Isa told us, who said: Musa ibn Abi Habib told us, who said: I heard al-Hakam ibn Umayr al-Thumali—and he had companionship with the Prophet—say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "This Qur'an is difficult, hard to grasp, heavy upon those who abandon it, and easy for those who follow and seek it. My speech (ḥadīth) is also difficult, hard to grasp, and it is the ruling (al-ḥukm). Whoever holds fast to my speech and memorizes it, is saved along with the Qur'an. Whoever neglects the Qur'an and my speech loses this world and the Hereafter. You have been commanded to take my word, to hold fast to my command, and to follow my Sunna. Whoever is pleased with my word has been pleased with the Qur'an, and whoever mocks my word has mocked the Qur'an. Allah, glorified is He, said: ﴿Whatever the Messenger gives you, take it, and whatever he forbids you, refrain from it﴾" [253] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 18/17.]].

We were informed by al-Husayn, who said: Ibn Shanbah told us, who said: al-Firyabi and Ubayd Allah ibn Ahmad al-Kinani told us, both saying: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shayba told us, who said: Mu'awiya ibn Hisham told us, who said: Sufyan al-Thawri told us, from al-Ashtar, from Ibrahim, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid, who said: Abdullah ibn Mas'ud met a man in the state of *ihram*, wearing his clothes, and said: Take them off. The man said: Are you reciting to me a verse from the Book of Allah with this? He said: Yes: ﴿Whatever the Messenger gives you, take it, and whatever he forbids you, refrain from it﴾ [254].

﴿And fear Allah; indeed, Allah is severe in punishment.﴾

**Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 59, verses 8–10:**

﴿لِلْفُقَراءِ﴾ meaning: so that what Allah has granted to His Messenger (the *fay'*, spoils that came without battle) does not become a commodity circulating only among the rich among you, but is for ﴿the poor Emigrants, who were expelled from their homes and their property, seeking bounty from Allah and His good pleasure, and supporting Allah and His Messenger. Those are the truthful﴾ in their faith.

Qatadah said: These are the Emigrants who left behind their homes, their wealth, their families and their kin, and went out out of love for Allah and His Messenger, choosing Islam despite the hardship they endured. It has been related to us that a man would tie a stone around his belly to keep his spine upright from hunger, and a man would dig a pit in winter, having no covering other than it.

Ja'far ibn al-Mughirah related, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Sa'id ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abza, who both said: Some of the Emigrants had a house, a wife, a servant and a camel, upon which he performed the Hajj and went out to fight. Yet Allah described them as poor, and assigned them a share of the *zakat* (obligatory alms).

﴿وَالَّذِينَ تَبَوَّؤُا﴾: they settled in the abode, i.e., they made Medina the abode of faith and emigration. These are the Ansar (the Helpers). They embraced Islam in their own homes and built mosques two years before the Prophet ﷺ arrived, so Allah deferred the building (of their own homes) for them.

The sense of the verse: ﴿and those who settled in the abode and in faith before them﴾, i.e., before the Emigrants came to them, ﴿love those who emigrated to them, and do not find in their breasts any need (*hazazah*, resentment) or anger or envy for what they were given﴾, i.e., for what they had given to the Emigrants from the *fay'*.

That is because the Messenger of Allah ﷺ divided the property of the Banu al-Nadir among the Emigrants, and gave none of it to the Ansar except three men, as we have mentioned. Yet the souls of the Ansar were content with that.

﴿and they prefer [them] over themselves﴾: they preferred their Emigrant brothers with their wealth and their homes, ﴿even though they themselves were in privation (*khasasah*): need and want for what is perishable﴾. That is because they shared their homes and their wealth with them.

Abu Muhammad al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Sijistani informed us, saying: Abu al-Abbas Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Thaqafi told us, saying: Mahmud ibn Khidash informed us, and I heard him say: I never took anything to buy [*] [[Thus is his wording in the manuscript; the report transmitted from him in the biographical works is: "I never bought anything nor sold." See Tahdhib al-Tahdhib 10: 56/102; Tarikh Baghdad 13: 91/7074.]] — he said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Sijistani told us, saying: al-Fudayl ibn Ghazwan told us, from Abu Hazim, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ, and hunger had afflicted him, and he said: O Messenger of Allah, I am hungry, so feed me.

The Prophet ﷺ (peace be upon him) sent to his wives: "Do you have anything?" All of them said: "By the One who sent you with the truth as a prophet, we have nothing except water." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The Messenger of Allah has nothing to feed you this night."

Then he said: "Whoever hosts this man tonight, may Allah have mercy on him." [[Zad al-Masir: 7/338.]] [255].

A man from the Ansar stood up and said: "I, O Messenger of Allah." He brought him to his home and said to his wife: "This is the guest of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; honor him and withhold nothing from him." She said: "We have nothing except the food of the children." He said: "Go and distract the children from their food until they sleep without having eaten anything. Then light the lamp and bring it out. When the guest takes to eat, go as though you are adjusting the lamp, and extinguish it. Then come, and let us move our tongues [as if chewing] for the guest of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, until the guest of the Messenger of Allah is satisfied."

She went to the children and distracted them until they slept without their food, then she rose, brought out the food and lit the lamp. When the guest took to eat, she rose as though adjusting the lamp and extinguished it, and the two of them began moving their tongues for the guest of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him). The guest thought they were eating with him, until the guest of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was satisfied, and the two of them spent the night hungry.

When they awoke in the morning, they went to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him). When he looked at them, he smiled and said: "Allah has marveled at so-and-so and so-and-so this night." [256]. Then Allah, the Exalted, revealed:

﴿and they prefer [them] over themselves, even though they themselves were in privation﴾, the verse.

Anas ibn Malik said: A roasted sheep's head was given as a gift to one of the Companions, and he was in need. He sent it to a neighbor of his, who passed it to nine persons, then it returned to the first. So Allah, the Exalted, revealed: ﴿and they prefer [them] over themselves, even though they themselves were in privation﴾.

It is related from Abu al-Hasan al-Antaki that a gathering of some thirty-odd men came together at his place in a village near al-Rayy. They had a limited number of loaves which were not sufficient for all of them. They spread out the loaves, extinguished the lamp, and sat down to eat. When the food was removed, the food was still intact, for not one of them had eaten, out of preference for his companion.

It is related from Hudhayfah al-Adawi that he said: On the day of al-Yarmuk I set out to look for a cousin of mine, carrying some water, and I was saying: If he has any breath left, I will give him water and wipe his face. Then I found him, and I said: Shall I give you water? He gestured, meaning yes. Then a man was saying: "Ah!" My cousin gestured that I should take it to him. It was Hisham ibn al-As. I said: Shall I give you water? He heard another, who said: "Ah!" Hisham gestured that I should take it to him. I went to him, and he had died. Then I returned to Hisham, and he had died. Then I returned to my cousin, and he had died, may Allah have mercy on him.

I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Naysaburi say: I heard Abu Abd Allah Muhammad ibn Ubayd Allah al-Jurjani say: I heard al-Hasan ibn Alawiyyah al-Damghani relate from Abu Yazid al-Bistami, who said: No one ever overcame me as a young man from the people of Balkh overcame me. He came to us as a pilgrim and said to me: "O Abu Yazid, what is the limit of asceticism (*zuhd*) among you?" I said: "When we find, we eat; and when we lack, we are patient." He said: "This is how the dogs of Balkh are with us." I said: "What is the limit of asceticism among you?" He said: "When we lack, we are patient; and when we find, we prefer [others]."

I also heard Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi say: I heard Abu Muhammad Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Baladhuri say: I heard Bakr ibn Abd al-Rahman say: Dhu al-Nun al-Misri was asked about the sign of the ascetic whose breast has been expanded, and he said: Three: dispersing what has been accumulated, leaving off the pursuit of what has been lost, and preferring others when one has provision.

Ibn Abbas said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said on the day of al-Nadir to the Ansar: "If you wish, you may divide for the Emigrants from your wealth and your homes, and they will share with you in this spoil. And if you wish, your homes and your wealth will remain yours, and nothing of the spoil will be divided for you." [257] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 9/430.]].

The Ansar said: "Rather, we will divide with them from our wealth and our homes, and we will prefer them in the division, and we will not share with them in it."

So Allah, the Exalted, revealed: ﴿and they prefer [them] over themselves, even though they themselves were in privation. And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his own soul, those are the successful﴾.

In the language of the Arabs, *shuhh* (stinginess) means miserliness and withholding excess. It is said: "So-and-so is *shahih*," from *al-shahh*, *al-shuhh*, *al-shahhah* and *al-shahahah*. 'Amr ibn Kulthum said:

*You see the stingy miser, when it is pressed upon him, humbled before his wealth* [[Lisan al-Arab: 5/404.]].

The scholars of the early generations distinguished between them.

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad informed me, saying: Musa ibn Muhammad ibn Ali told us, saying: Idris ibn Abd al-Karim al-Haddad told us, saying: Asim ibn Ali ibn Asim told us; and Abd al-Khaliq informed us, saying: Ibn Habib told us, saying: Ibn Shakir told us, saying: Asim ibn Ali told us, saying: al-Ma'adi told us, from Jami' ibn Shaddad, from Abu al-Sha'tha', who said:

A man said to Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud: "O Abu Abd al-Rahman, I fear that I have perished." He said: "And what is that?" He said: "I heard Allah, the Exalted, say: *And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his own soul*, and I am a stingy man; hardly anything leaves my hands." He said: "That is not the *shuhh* which Allah, the Exalted, mentioned in the Qur'an. Rather, *shuhh* is that you consume your brother's wealth unjustly. That is merely *bukhl* (miserliness), and miserliness is a wretched thing."

Al-Walibi: Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿whoever is protected from the stinginess of his own soul﴾, said: It means: the desire of his soul, following its whims, so he did not accept faith.

Ibn Zayd said: Whoever does not take anything that Allah, the Exalted, has forbidden him, and whose *shuhh* does not prevent him from withholding anything that Allah, the Exalted, has commanded him to give, has been protected from the stinginess of his own soul.

Tawus said: *Bukhl* is that a person is stingy with what is in his own hands, and *shuhh* is that he is stingy with what is in the hands of people.

My father informed me, saying: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nahwi informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Hamdun ibn Khalid informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab ibn Abi Tammam al-Asqalani told us, saying: Sulayman ibn Bint Shurahil told us, saying: Isma'il ibn Abbas told us, saying: Umarah ibn Adiyyah al-Ansari told us, from his paternal uncle Umar ibn Jariyah, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "He is free from *shuhh* who pays the *zakat*, hosts the guest, and gives in times of calamity." [258] [[al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: 4/188.]].

Abu Abd Allah al-Hafiz informed me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Abd Allah ibn Muhammad al-Ta'i informed us, saying: Abd Allah ibn Zayd told us, saying: Ibrahim ibn al-Ala' told us, saying: Isma'il ibn Abbas told us, from Hisham ibn al-Ghad, from Aban, from Anas, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to supplicate: "O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the stinginess of my soul, its excess, and its whisperings." [259] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 18/30.]].

Abu Abd Allah informed us, saying: Harun ibn Muhammad ibn Harun told us, saying: Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Sinan informed us, saying: Abd Allah ibn Maslamah al-Qa'nabi told us, saying: Dawud ibn Qays al-Farra' told us, from Abd Allah ibn Muqsim, from Jabir ibn Abd Allah, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Beware of *shuhh*, for *shuhh* destroyed those before you; it drove them to shed their blood and make lawful what was forbidden to them." [260] [[Musnad Ahmad: 3/323.]].

Sa'id ibn Jubayr related, from Abu al-Hayyaj al-Asadi, who said: I was circumambulating the House, and I saw a man saying: "O Allah, protect me from the stinginess of my soul," and he would not add anything to that. I asked him about it, and he said: "When I am protected from the stinginess of my soul, I do not steal, I do not commit adultery, and I do not do such things." And the man was Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf.

It is related that Kisra said to his companions: "What is the thing most harmful to the son of Adam?" They said: "Poverty." Kisra said: "Stinginess is more harmful than poverty, because the poor man, when he finds, becomes expansive, but the stingy man never becomes expansive."

﴿and those who came after them say: Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith, and do not place in our hearts any resentment toward those who have believed. Our Lord, You are indeed Kind and Merciful﴾.

Ibn Abi Layla said: People are of three ranks: the poor Emigrants; ﴿those who settled in the abode and in faith﴾, ...; and ﴿those who came after them﴾. So strive that you not be outside these ranks.

Al-Hasan informed me, saying: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Mawsili told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Makhlad al-Duri told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Hassani told us, saying: Abu Yahya al-Hammani related to me, from al-Hasan ibn Umarah, from al-Hakam ibn Utaybah, from Miqsam, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Allah, the Exalted, commanded seeking forgiveness for the Companions of Muhammad ﷺ, while He knew that they would be tested.

Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn Abd Allah told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Sulayman told us, saying: Ibn Numayr told us, saying: my father told us, from Isma'il ibn Ibrahim, from Abd al-Malik ibn Umayr, from Masruq, from Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her), who said: You were commanded to seek forgiveness for the Companions of Muhammad ﷺ, but you reviled them. I heard your Prophet ﷺ say: "This Ummah will not perish until its last generation curses its first." [261] [[al-Mu'jam al-Awsat: 5/255, where it reads "will be annihilated" (tufna) instead of "will not perish" (la tadhhab); and Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 18/33.]].

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Abd Allah ibn Yusuf told us, saying: al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Tusi told us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Mu'ammal ibn al-Sabbah al-Basri told us, saying: al-Nadr ibn Hammad al-Ataki told us, saying:

Sayf ibn Umar al-Asadi told us, saying: Ubayd Allah ibn Umar told us, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When you see those who revile my Companions, say: May Allah curse your evil." [262] [[al-Mu'jam al-Awsat: 8/191.]].

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: al-Fadl ibn al-Fadl al-Kindi told us, saying: Ibn al-Nu'man told us, saying:

Harun ibn Sulayman told us, saying: Abd Allah, meaning Ibn Dawud, told us, saying: Kathir ibn Marwan al-Shami told us, from Abd Allah ibn Yazid al-Dimashqi, who said: I came to al-Hasan and he mentioned words, except that he said: I encountered three hundred of the Companions of Muhammad ﷺ, seventy of whom were from Badr, all of whom related to me that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever separates from the community by a span has removed the bond of Islam from his neck." [263] [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi: 4/226.]].

So the community (*al-jama'ah*) means: not reviling the Companions, not disputing about the religion of Allah, and not declaring anyone among the People of Monotheism to be a disbeliever for a sin.

Abd Allah ibn Zayd said: I met Abu Umamah, Abu al-Darda', Wathilah and Anas ibn Malik, and all of them related to me a hadith from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ like the hadith of the community.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Habish told us, saying: Abu al-Fadl Salih ibn al-Asbagh al-Tanukhi told us, saying: Abu al-Fadl al-Rabi' ibn Muhammad ibn Isa al-Kindi told us, saying: Sa'id ibn Mansur told us, saying: Shihab ibn Hirash told us, from his paternal uncle al-Awwam ibn Hawshab, who said: I met those whom I met from the early part of this Ummah, and they used to say: "Mention the virtues of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so that hearts may be united upon them, and do not mention what occurred among them, lest you incite people against them."

I heard Abd Allah ibn Hamid say: I heard Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan say: I heard Abu Abd Allah Muhammad ibn al-Qasim al-Jumahi al-Makki say: I heard Muhammad ibn Sa'dan al-Marwazi say: I heard Ahmad ibn Isma'il al-Marwazi, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Malik ibn Mighwal, from his father, who said: Amir ibn Shurahil al-Sha'bi said: "O Malik, the Jews and the Christians have surpassed the Rafidah in one quality. The Jews were asked: Who is the best of the people of your religion? They said: The companions of Musa. The Christians were asked: Who is the best of the people of your religion? They said: The disciples of Isa. And the Rafidah were asked: Who is the worst of the people of your religion? They said: The Companions of Muhammad. They were commanded to seek forgiveness for them, but they reviled them. So the sword is drawn against them until the Day of Resurrection; no banner rises for them, no foot is firm for them, and no word is united for them. *Every time they kindle a fire for war, Allah extinguishes it*, through the shedding of their blood, the scattering of their unity, and the refutation of their argument. May Allah protect us and you from misguiding desires."

Abu al-Hasan Abd al-Rahman ibn Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Mu'addil informed us, saying: Abu Abd Allah Muhammad ibn Yunus al-Muqri told us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Salim told us, saying: Sawwar ibn Abd Allah al-Qadi told us, saying: my father told us, saying: Malik ibn Anas said: Whoever belittles any of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and there is resentment in his heart toward them, has no right to the spoils of the Muslims. Then he recited ﴿what Allah has granted to His Messenger from the people of the towns﴾, until he reached this verse; then he recited ﴿for the poor﴾ until he reached this verse; then he said: ﴿and those who settled in the abode and in faith﴾ until he reached this verse; then he said: ﴿and those who came after them﴾ up to His saying: ﴿Kind and Merciful﴾. So whoever belittles them, or has resentment in his heart toward them, has no right to the spoils.

I said: Shall I give you water? He heard another, who said: "Ah!" Hisham gestured that I should take it to him. I went to him, and he had died. Then I returned to Hisham, and he had died. Then I returned to my cousin, and he had died, may Allah have mercy on him.

I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Naysaburi say: I heard Abu Abd Allah Muhammad ibn Ubayd Allah al-Jurjani say: I heard al-Hasan ibn Alawiyyah al-Damghani relate from Abu Yazid al-Bistami, who said: No one ever overcame me as a young man from the people of Balkh overcame me. He came to us as a pilgrim and said to me: "O Abu Yazid, what is the limit of asceticism (*zuhd*) among you?" I said: "When we find, we eat; and when we lack, we are patient." He said: "This is how the dogs of Balkh are with us." I said: "What is the limit of asceticism among you?" He said: "When we lack, we are patient; and when we find, we prefer [others]."

I also heard Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi say: I heard Abu Muhammad Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Baladhuri say: I heard Bakr ibn Abd al-Rahman say: Dhu al-Nun al-Misri was asked about the sign of the ascetic whose breast has been expanded, and he said: Three: dispersing what has been accumulated, leaving off the pursuit of what has been lost, and preferring others when one has provision.

Ibn Abbas said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said on the day of al-Nadir to the Ansar: "If you wish, you may divide for the Emigrants from your wealth and your homes, and they will share with you in this spoil. And if you wish, your homes and your wealth will remain yours, and nothing of the spoil will be divided for you." [257] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 9/430.]].

The Ansar said: "Rather, we will divide with them from our wealth and our homes, and we will prefer them in the division, and we will not share with them in it."

So Allah, the Exalted, revealed: ﴿and they prefer [them] over themselves, even though they themselves were in privation. And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his own soul, those are the successful﴾.

In the language of the Arabs, *shuhh* (stinginess) means miserliness and withholding excess. It is said: "So-and-so is *shahih*," from *al-shahh*, *al-shuhh*, *al-shahhah* and *al-shahahah*. 'Amr ibn Kulthum said:

*You see the stingy miser, when it is pressed upon him, humbled before his wealth* [[Lisan al-Arab: 5/404.]].

The scholars of the early generations distinguished between them.

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad informed me, saying: Musa ibn Muhammad ibn Ali told us, saying: Idris ibn Abd al-Karim al-Haddad told us, saying: Asim ibn Ali ibn Asim told us; and Abd al-Khaliq informed us, saying: Ibn Habib told us, saying: Ibn Shakir told us, saying: Asim ibn Ali told us, saying: al-Ma'adi told us, from Jami' ibn Shaddad, from Abu al-Sha'tha', who said:

A man said to Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud: "O Abu Abd al-Rahman, I fear that I have perished." He said: "And what is that?" He said: "That is not the *shuhh* which Allah, the Exalted, mentioned in the Qur'an. Rather, *shuhh* is that you consume your brother's wealth unjustly. That is merely *bukhl* (miserliness), and miserliness is a wretched thing."

Al-Walibi: Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿whoever is protected from the stinginess of his own soul﴾, said: It means: the desire of his soul, following its whims, so he did not accept faith.

Ibn Zayd said: Whoever does not take anything that Allah, the Exalted, has forbidden him, and whose *shuhh* does not prevent him from withholding anything that Allah, the Exalted, has commanded him to give, has been protected from the stinginess of his own soul.

Tawus said: *Bukhl* is that a person is stingy with what is in his own hands, and *shuhh* is that he is stingy with what is in the hands of people.

﴿and those who came after them say: Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith, and do not place in our hearts any resentment toward those who have believed. Our Lord, You are indeed Kind and Merciful﴾.

[263] [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi: 4/226.]].

I heard Abd Allah ibn Hamid say: I heard Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan say: I heard Abu Abd Allah Muhammad ibn al-Qasim al-Jumahi al-Makki say: I heard Muhammad ibn Sa'dan al-Marwazi say: I heard Ahmad ibn Isma'il al-Marwazi, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Malik ibn Mighwal, from his father, who said: Amir ibn Shurahil al-Sha'bi said: "O Malik, the Jews and the Christians have surpassed the Rafidah in one quality. Then he recited ﴿what Allah has granted to His Messenger from the people of the towns﴾, until he reached this verse; then he recited ﴿for the poor﴾ until he reached this verse; then he said: ﴿and those who settled in the abode and in faith﴾ until he reached this verse; then he said: ﴿and those who came after them﴾ up to His saying: ﴿Kind and Merciful﴾. So whoever belittles them, or has resentment in his heart toward them, has no right to the spoils.

**Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 59, verses 8–10:**

﴿لِلْفُقَراءِ﴾ meaning: so that what Allah has granted to His Messenger (the *fay'*, spoils that came without battle) does not become a commodity circulating only among the rich among you, but is for ﴿the poor Emigrants, who were expelled from their homes and their property, seeking bounty from Allah and His good pleasure, and supporting Allah and His Messenger. Those are the truthful﴾ in their faith.

Qatadah said: These are the Emigrants who left behind their homes, their wealth, their families and their kin, and went out out of love for Allah and His Messenger, choosing Islam despite the hardship they endured. It has been related to us that a man would tie a stone around his belly to keep his spine upright from hunger, and a man would dig a pit in winter, having no covering other than it.

Ja'far ibn al-Mughirah related, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Sa'id ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abza, who both said: Some of the Emigrants had a house, a wife, a servant and a camel, upon which he performed the Hajj and went out to fight. Yet Allah described them as poor, and assigned them a share of the *zakat* (obligatory alms).

﴿وَالَّذِينَ تَبَوَّؤُا﴾: they settled in the abode, i.e., they made Medina the abode of faith and emigration. These are the Ansar (the Helpers). They embraced Islam in their own homes and built mosques two years before the Prophet ﷺ arrived, so Allah deferred the building (of their own homes) for them.

The sense of the verse: ﴿and those who settled in the abode and in faith before them﴾, i.e., before the Emigrants came to them, ﴿love those who emigrated to them, and do not find in their breasts any need (*hazazah*, resentment) or anger or envy for what they were given﴾, i.e., for what they had given to the Emigrants from the *fay'*.

That is because the Messenger of Allah ﷺ divided the property of the Banu al-Nadir among the Emigrants, and gave none of it to the Ansar except three men, as we have mentioned. Yet the souls of the Ansar were content with that.

﴿and they prefer [them] over themselves﴾: they preferred their Emigrant brothers with their wealth and their homes, ﴿even though they themselves were in privation (*khasasah*): need and want for what is perishable﴾. That is because they shared their homes and their wealth with them.

Abu Muhammad al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Sijistani informed us, saying: Abu al-Abbas Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Thaqafi told us, saying: Mahmud ibn Khidash informed us, and I heard him say: I never took anything to buy [*] [[Thus is his wording in the manuscript; the report transmitted from him in the biographical works is: "I never bought anything nor sold." See Tahdhib al-Tahdhib 10: 56/102; Tarikh Baghdad 13: 91/7074.]] — he said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Sijistani told us, saying: al-Fudayl ibn Ghazwan told us, from Abu Hazim, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ, and hunger had afflicted him, and he said: O Messenger of Allah, I am hungry, so feed me.

The Prophet ﷺ (peace be upon him) sent to his wives: "Do you have anything?" All of them said: "By the One who sent you with the truth as a prophet, we have nothing except water." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The Messenger of Allah has nothing to feed you this night."

Then he said: "Whoever hosts this man tonight, may Allah have mercy on him." [[Zad al-Masir: 7/338.]] [255].

A man from the Ansar stood up and said: "I, O Messenger of Allah." He brought him to his home and said to his wife: "This is the guest of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; honor him and withhold nothing from him." She said: "We have nothing except the food of the children." He said: "Go and distract the children from their food until they sleep without having eaten anything. Then light the lamp and bring it out. When the guest takes to eat, go as though you are adjusting the lamp, and extinguish it. Then come, and let us move our tongues [as if chewing] for the guest of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, until the guest of the Messenger of Allah is satisfied."

She went to the children and distracted them until they slept without their food, then she rose, brought out the food and lit the lamp. When the guest took to eat, she rose as though adjusting the lamp and extinguished it, and the two of them began moving their tongues for the guest of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him). The guest thought they were eating with him, until the guest of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was satisfied, and the two of them spent the night hungry.

When they awoke in the morning, they went to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him). When he looked at them, he smiled and said: "Allah has marveled at so-and-so and so-and-so this night." [256]. Then Allah, the Exalted, revealed:

﴿and they prefer [them] over themselves, even though they themselves were in privation﴾, the verse.

Anas ibn Malik said: A roasted sheep's head was given as a gift to one of the Companions, and he was in need. He sent it to a neighbor of his, who passed it to nine persons, then it returned to the first. So Allah, the Exalted, revealed: ﴿and they prefer [them] over themselves, even though they themselves were in privation﴾.

It is related from Abu al-Hasan al-Antaki that a gathering of some thirty-odd men came together at his place in a village near al-Rayy. They had a limited number of loaves which were not sufficient for all of them. They spread out the loaves, extinguished the lamp, and sat down to eat. When the food was removed, the food was still intact, for not one of them had eaten, out of preference for his companion.
