[A word is missing in the manuscript; what is supplied is the likely reading.] One of the wise men was asked about the meaning of *al-Jabbar*, and he said: He is the Subduer who, when He wills a matter, does it and decides in it what He wills; no barrier restrains Him from it, and He does not consider anyone below Him. Adam was chosen without obedience, and Iblis was cursed despite much obedience. It was also said: He is the one whom hands cannot reach, from the saying of the Arabs: a *jabbara* palm, when it grows tall and hands cannot reach it. The poet said:

*"Lofty-stemmed, with dense branches, and bearing red clusters of dates."*

[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 18/47.]

﴿Al-Mutakabbir,﴾ exalted above every evil, glorifying Himself above what is not befitting Him. The root of *al-kibr* and *al-kibriya'* is refusal and unwillingness to submit. Humayd ibn Thawr said:

*"It has been effaced as the weaned calf effaces, so the pride of the stubborn one has become a tame mount."*

[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 18/47; Lisan al-'Arab: 12/431, where the text reads "al-tali" instead of "al-fasil" and "rukub" instead of "dhalul."]

﴿Al-Khaliq,﴾ the Determiner, the one who transforms a thing through arrangement into another, as He said: ﴿He creates you within the wombs of your mothers, creation after creation﴾ [Surah al-Zumar: 6], and He said: ﴿He created you in stages﴾ [Surah Nuh: 14]. ﴿Al-Bari',﴾ the Originator of entities from nonexistence into existence. ﴿Al-Musawwir,﴾ the One who gives form to created things, marks, distinguishing features, and differing shapes, so that some are distinguished from others. It is said: "This is the image of the matter," meaning its likeness. First it is a creation, then a drop, then a clot, then, when it is complete and perfected, a form. And Allah knows best.

﴿To Him belong the best names. Whatever is in the heavens and the earth glorifies Him, and He is the Almighty, the Wise.﴾

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Faqih informed us in al-Qasr: Isma'il ibn Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us in Baghdad: al-Hasan ibn 'Arafa related to us: Muhammad ibn Salih al-Wasiti related to us, from Sulayman ibn Muhammad, from 'Umar ibn Nafi', from his father, who said: 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar said: "I saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) standing on this pulpit, meaning the pulpit of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), relating from his Lord, Glorified, and he said: 'When the Day of Resurrection comes, Allah, the Exalted, will gather the seven heavens and the earths in His grip, blessed and exalted. Then He will say, [making a gesture] like this, and He will tighten His grip, then open it. Then He will say: I am Allah. I am the Most Merciful. I am the Especially Merciful. I am the King. I am the Pure. I am the Giver of Security. I am the Granter of Safety. I am the Protector. I am the Mighty. I am the Compeller. I am the Supreme. I am the One who began the world when it was nothing. I am the One who will restore it. Where are the kings? Where are the tyrants?'"

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me: Ibn Wahb related to us: Muhammad ibn Yunus al-Karimi related to us: 'Amr ibn 'Asim related to us: Abu al-Ashhab related to us, from Yazid ibn Aban, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites the end of Surat al-Hashr, his past sins and his future sins will be forgiven."

And Ibn Fanjawayh informed me: Ibn Shanba related to us: Ibn Wahb related to us: Ahmad ibn Abi Surayj and Ahmad ibn Mansur al-Ramadi related to us, both saying: Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri related to us: Khalid ibn Sulayman related to us: Nafi' related to me, from Abu Nafi', from Ma'qil ibn Yasar, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever says, when he wakes in the morning, three times: 'I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Shaytan,' and recites three verses from the end of Surat al-Hashr, Allah will assign to him seventy thousand angels who will send blessings upon him until evening. If he dies that day, he dies as a martyr. And whoever says it in the evening has the same status."

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 59, verse 11–24 (part 2 of 2):

It was related to me by Muhammad ibn al-Qasim, who said: Abdullah ibn Muhammad told us, who said: al-Samah told us, who said: Ahmad ibn al-Farah told us, who said: Abu Uthman, that is, the muezzin, told us, who said: Muhammad ibn Ziyad told us, who said: I heard Abu Umamah say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites the final verses of Surat al-Hashr by night or by day, and dies on that day or that night, has certainly earned Paradise." [267] [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 1/583, no. 2643.]]

And it was related to me by Ibn al-Qasim, who said: Ibn Bakhtiyar told us, who said: Makki ibn 'Aydan told us, who said: Ibrahim ibn Abdullah told us, who said: Amr ibn 'Asim told us, who said: Abu al-Ashhab told us, who said: Yazid al-Raqqashi related to us from Anas that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites the last surah of al-Hashr: ﴿Had We sent down this Qur'an upon a mountain…﴾ to its end, and dies that night, dies as a martyr." [268] [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 1/593, no. 2703.]]

And it was related to me by Abu Uthman ibn Abi Bakr al-Habari, who said: Abu al-Husayn Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Hajjaji told us, who said: Abdullah ibn Aban ibn Shaddad informed us that Isma'il ibn Muhammad al-Habarini related to them, who said:
Ali ibn Zuraiq told us, who said: Hisham related to us from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Ata' ibn Yasar, from Abu Hurairah, who said:
I asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about the Greatest Name of Allah, and he said: "Keep to the final verses of Surat al-Hashr and recite them often." So I repeated the question, and he repeated the answer to me; I asked again, and he answered me again. [269] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 18/49.]]

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 59, verses 11–24 (part 1 of 2):

﴿Have you not considered those who played the hypocrite,﴾ meaning they displayed the opposite of what they concealed. The word is derived from *nafiqa'* (the hypocrite's escape hole of the jerboa, *nafiqa' al-yarbu'*), which is the jerboa's burrow exit. When a jerboa's one exit is blocked, it digs out another, and so it is said at that point: *nafaqa* and *naafaqa*. The hypocrite's conduct is likened to the jerboa's, because it enters by one door and leaves by another: the hypocrite enters Islam with his tongue and leaves it with his belief. The term *nifaq* (hypocrisy) is an Islamic term that the Arabs did not know before Islam.

﴿They say to their brothers who disbelieved from among the People of the Book,﴾ namely the Banu Qurayza and the Banu al-Nadir, ﴿"If you are expelled, we will certainly go out with you, and we will never obey anyone against you. And if you are fought, we will surely support you." And Allah testifies that they are liars. ﴿If they are expelled, they will not go out with them; and if they are fought, they will not support them; and if they support them, they will surely turn their backs; then they will not be helped.﴾ ﴿Indeed, you [O assembly of believers] are more fearsome in their breasts than Allah.﴾ It means: they fear you more than they fear Allah. ﴿That is because they are a people who do not understand.﴾ ﴿They will not fight you all together except within fortified towns or from behind walls.﴾ That is, the Jews will not fight you openly.

Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Ibn Kathir and Abu 'Amr read (*judar*), with an alif, in the singular.

It is reported from some people of Makkah: (*jadr*), with a fatha on the *jim* and a sukun on the *dal*, which is a dialect form of *jidar* (wall).

Yahya ibn Wathhab read (*judr*), with a damma on the *jim* and a sukun on the *dal*.

The rest read both with damma.

﴿Their violence among themselves is severe.﴾ That is: some of them are harsh toward others, and some are enemies to others, and their enmity toward one another is intense.

It was also said: their violence among themselves, from behind walls and fortresses, is severe; but when they come out against you, they are the most cowardly of Allah's creation.

﴿You think they are united, but their hearts are divided.﴾ Scattered and disunited. Qatada said: the people of falsehood have divergent desires, divergent testimonies, and divergent deeds, yet they are united in enmity toward the people of truth. Mujahid said: it means that the religion of the hypocrites differs from the religion of the Jews. ﴿That is because they are a people who do not reason.﴾ ﴿Like those before them, shortly before, they tasted the consequence of their affair.﴾ That is, the likeness of these is the likeness of those before them, namely the polytheists of Makkah. Mujahid said: "shortly before" refers to the Battle of Badr. Ibn 'Abbas said: "like those before them" refers to the Banu Qaynuqa'. It was also said: the likeness of Qurayza is the likeness of the Banu al-Nadir, and there were two years between them. Thus they tasted the consequence of their affair, which was exile and banishment. ﴿And for them is a painful punishment.﴾

Then Allah struck a parable for the hypocrites and the Jews in their abandonment of one another, and He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Like the Shaytan when he says to man, "Disbelieve," ...﴾ (the verse).

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me: al-Baqarihi related to us: al-Hasan ibn 'Alawiyya related to us: Isma'il ibn 'Isa related to us: Ishaq ibn Bishr related to us: Muqatil related to us, from 'Ata', from Ibn 'Abbas, and from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying, ﴿Like the Shaytan when he says to man, "Disbelieve." And when he disbelieves, he says, "Indeed, I am free of you ..."﴾ (the verse). He said: There was a monk in the interval (between prophets) called Barsisa. He had worshipped in his hermitage for seventy years without disobeying Allah even for the blink of an eye. Iblis was unable to overcome him by any of his schemes and could not prevail over him. So one day he gathered the rebellious devils and said: "Is there none among you who will suffice me against Barsisa's affair?" Al-Abyad, who is the companion of the prophets and who confronts the Prophet (ﷺ), said: "I will suffice you." He came to the Prophet (ﷺ) in the form of Gabriel in order to whisper to him in the manner of revelation. Then Gabriel came and stood between them and pushed him with his hand, a gentle push, and he fell from Gabriel's push to the farthest land of India. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿Possessor of power, with the Lord of the Throne secure, obeyed there [and trustworthy]﴾ [Surah al-Takwir: 20].

Al-Abyad said to Iblis: "I will suffice you." So he went, adorned himself with the adornment of monks, shaved the middle of his head, and went until he came to Barsisa's hermitage. He called out to him, but Barsisa did not answer him. Barsisa would not turn away from his prayer except once every ten days, and would not break his fast except once every ten days. He would fast for ten days, twenty days, or longer. When al-Abyad saw that he would not answer him, he devoted himself to worship at the base of the hermitage. When Barsisa finished his prayer, he looked out from his hermitage and saw al-Abyad standing, praying in a good form of monastic conduct. When he saw this from him, he regretted that he had turned away from him and had not answered him. So he said to him: "You called me, and I was occupied away from you. What is your need?"

He said: "My need is that I would like to be with you, so that I may call upon you, gain knowledge from you, and we may gather in worship, so that you may supplicate for me and I may supplicate for you." Barsisa said: "I am indeed busy away from you. If you are a believer, Allah, Glorified, will surely make for you a share in what I supplicate for the believing men and women, if He answers me." Then he turned to his prayer and left al-Abyad. Al-Abyad began to pray, and Barsisa did not turn toward him for forty days after that. When he finished, he saw him standing and praying. When Barsisa saw the intensity of his striving, the abundance of his humility, and his supplication to Allah, Glorified, he spoke to him and said:

"What is your need?"

He said: "My need is that you permit me to come up to you." He permitted him, and he came up to him in his hermitage. Al-Abyad remained with him for a year, worshipping, breaking his fast only once every forty days, and turning from his prayer only once every forty days; at times he extended it to eighty. When Barsisa saw his striving, his soul was drawn to him, and the affair of al-Abyad impressed him. When the year had passed, al-Abyad said to Barsisa: "I am departing, for I have another companion other than you. I thought you were more diligent than I see you to be, and what reached us about you was other than what I have seen." He said: So a severe matter entered Barsisa's heart, and he disliked parting from him because of what he had seen of his intense striving. When he bade him farewell, al-Abyad said to him: "I have supplications that I will teach you; call upon Him with them, for they are better than what you are in. Allah will heal the sick through them, and will restore well-being to the afflicted and the possessed." Barsisa said: "I dislike this position, because I have a concern within myself, and I fear that if people know of this, they will occupy me away from worship." Al-Abyad kept at him until he taught him. Then he went and came to Iblis and said to him: "By Allah, you have ruined the man." He said: Then al-Abyad went and encountered a man, strangled him, and then came to him in the form of a physician and said to his family:

"Your companion has madness. Shall I treat him?"

They said: "Yes." He said to them: "I am not able to overcome his jinn, but I will direct you to one who supplicates to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and he will be granted healing." They said to him: "Guide us." So they went to Barsisa, saying: "Indeed, with him is the Name of Allah, which when called upon, He answers." He said: So they went to him and asked him for that, and he supplicated with those words, and the devil departed from the man. Al-Abyad used to do this with people similarly. Then Iblis came to Barsisa in the form of a man and said: "Your need is with me ..."

Barsisa said: "What is it?" He said: "Prostrate to me." He said: "I will do so." So he prostrated to him. He said: "O Barsisa, this is what I wanted from you. The outcome of your affair has become that you disbelieved in your Lord." When he disbelieved, he said, ﴿Indeed, I am free of you. Indeed, I fear Allah, Lord of the worlds.﴾ Allah, Glorified, says: ﴿So the outcome for both of them,﴾ meaning the Shaytan and that man, ﴿was that they would be in the Fire, abiding eternally therein. And that is the recompense of the wrongdoers.﴾

Ibn 'Abbas said: Allah struck this parable for the Jews of the Banu al-Nadir and the hypocrites of Madinah, and that is because Allah, Glorified, commanded His Prophet (peace be upon him) to expel the Banu al-Nadir from Madinah. The hypocrites secretly sent word to them, saying: "Do not respond to Muhammad in what he calls you to, and do not leave your homes, for if he fights you, we will be with you, and if he expels you, we will go out with you." He said: So they obeyed them, and they fortified their strongholds and secured themselves in their homes, hoping for the hypocrites' support. Until the Prophet (ﷺ) came to them and they set themselves against him in war, hoping for the hypocrites' support, but the hypocrites forsook them and disowned them, just as the Shaytan disowned Barsisa and forsook him.

Ibn 'Abbas said: After that, the monks among the Children of Israel would walk only in dissimulation and concealment. The people of depravity and wickedness coveted the rabbis, so they accused them with slander and vile things, until the matter of Jurayj the monk arose. When Allah cleared Jurayj the monk of what they had accused him of, the monks then felt at ease and appeared openly before the people.

﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah by performing His obligations and avoiding His prohibitions, and let every soul look to what it has put forward for tomorrow,﴾ meaning the Day of Resurrection. ﴿And fear Allah; indeed, Allah is Acquainted with what you do.﴾ ﴿And do not be like those who forgot Allah, so He made them forget themselves.﴾ That is, they forgot the right of Allah and abandoned His command, so He made them forget their own share, that they should send forward good for themselves. ﴿Those are the defiantly disobedient.﴾ ﴿The companions of the Fire and the companions of Paradise are not equal. The companions of Paradise are the attainers of success.﴾ ﴿If We had sent down this Qur'an upon a mountain, and had placed in it reason, you would have seen it humbled, split apart from the fear of Allah.﴾ That is, in its hardness and firmness, humbly submissive, cracking open out of fear of Allah. ﴿And these examples We present to the people, that they may give thought.﴾ ﴿He is Allah, other than whom there is no deity, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed.﴾ The unseen is what is hidden from the servants, what they have not witnessed and have not known; and the witnessed is what they have known and seen. Al-Hasan said: it means the secret and the public.

﴿He is the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful. He is Allah, other than whom there is no deity, the King.﴾ Al-Malik is the Possessor of dominion. It was also said: the One capable of originating things. ﴿The Pure, the Free from every defect, Who is exalted above what is not befitting Him.﴾ Qatada said: "al-Quddus" means "the Blessed." Ibn Kaysan said: "the Glorified," and in Syriac it is *qadisha*.

﴿The Giver of security, the Granter of safety.﴾ Some said: He who confirms His messengers by manifesting His miracles upon them, and who confirms for the believers what He has promised them of reward and accepts their faith, and who confirms for the disbelievers what He has threatened them of punishment.

Ibn 'Abbas and Muqatil said: He is the one who grants people security from His oppression, and grants security from His punishment to those who believe in Him, through this faith which is this fear, as He said: ﴿and gave them security from fear﴾ [Surah Quraysh: 4].

Al-Nabigha said:

*"And the Granter of security to the birds that seek refuge, whom the riders of Makkah wipe between the thicket and the mountain."*

[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 18/46. *al-'a'idhat* means the birds that have sought refuge in the House; *al-ghil* means the dense, intertwined trees; *al-sind* means what faces you of the mountain and rises high.]

Ibn Zayd said: He is the one who confirms the believers when they affirm His oneness. Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: He is the one who calls to faith, commands it, and makes it binding upon its people; His name. Al-Qurazi said: He is the Protector, as He said: ﴿And He protects, and none can protect against Him﴾ [Surah al-Mu'minun: 88].

﴿Al-Muhaymin.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid and Qatada said: the Witness. Al-Dahhak: the Trustworthy. Ibn Zayd: the Confirmer. Ibn Kaysan: it is one of the names of Allah in the scriptures; Allah knows its interpretation. 'Ata': the Trusted over His creation. Al-Khalil: the Watchful. Yaman: the Observer. Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab: the Judge.

Al-Mubarrad: [al-Muhaymin has the meaning of *mu'ayman*, except that the *ha'* replaces the hamza.]

Abu 'Ubayda said: There are five words in the Arabic language of this pattern: *al-muhaymin*, *al-musaytir*, *al-mubayti'*, *al-muniqir* (which is the one who goes away in the earth), and *al-mukhaymir*, which is the name of a mountain.

﴿Al-'Aziz, al-Jabbar.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: He is the Great, and *jabarut* (the divine dominion) of Allah is His greatness. According to this view, it is an attribute of His essence. It was also said: it derives from *al-jabr*, which is mending; one says, "I set the bone" when one mends it after a break, and "I restored the matter." *Jabara* and *jabbara* are both intransitive and transitive. Al-'Ajjaj said:

*"The God has mended the religion, so it was mended."*

The parallel in the speech of the Arabs: *dala'a lisanahu fa-dala'a* (he protruded his tongue, and it protruded), *faghara fahu fa-fagharat* (he opened his mouth, and it opened), and *'ammara al-dar fa-'ammarat* (he built up the house, and it was built up). Al-Suddi said: He is the one who subdues people and compels them to what He wills.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me: 'Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us: 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz al-Baghawi related to us: Muhammad ibn Bakkar ibn al-Rayyan related to us: Abu Ma'shar related to us, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b, who said: He is only called *al-Jabbar* because He compels creation to what He wills, and creation is too weak to disobey Him for even the blink of an eye except in what He wills. [A word is missing in the manuscript; what is supplied is the likely reading.] One of the wise men was asked about the meaning of *al-Jabbar*, and he said: He is the Subduer who, when He wills a matter, does it and decides in it what He wills; no barrier restrains Him from it, and He does not consider anyone below Him. Adam was chosen without obedience, and Iblis was cursed despite much obedience. It was also said: He is the one whom hands cannot reach, from the saying of the Arabs: a *jabbara* palm, when it grows tall and hands cannot reach it. The poet said:

*"Lofty-stemmed, with dense branches, and bearing red clusters of dates."*

[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 18/47.]
